title: A perfect complex on a quasi-compact open is a retract of a global restriction
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover, and the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Use its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C_X=D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Perfect means etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace], and let $A\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ be perfect. There exist a perfect $Q\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and morphisms $s:A\to i^*Q$, $r:i^*Q\to A$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ with $r\circ s=\mathrm{id}_A$. Here $i^*$ is exact restriction to the open small etale site [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

proof.text: Fix the given perfect $A$ on $U$. For a quasi-compact open $W\subset X$, let $\mathcal P(W)$ assert that $U\subset W$ and that there are a perfect $B$ on $W$ and maps $s_W:A\to B|_U$, $r_W:B|_U\to A$ with $r_Ws_W=\mathrm{id}_A$. At $W=U$ choose $B=A$ and both maps the identity. The enlargement induction principle reduces $\mathcal P(X)$ to its preservation across an elementary distinguished square $(W_1\subset W_2,f:V\to W_2)$ with $U\subset W_1$ and $V$ affine. Fix a witness $(B,s_1,r_1)$ for $\mathcal P(W_1)$. Its overlap $H=W_1\times_{W_2}V$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of $V$.

proof.text: Restriction of a local bounded complex of finite-free summands stays such a complex, so $F=B|_H$ is perfect. Since $H$ is a quasi-compact open of the affine scheme $V$, it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The quasi-coherence clause for perfect objects puts $F$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{H,\mathrm{et}})$. The etale/Zariski equivalence gives $F_0\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{H,\mathrm{Zar}})$ with $\epsilon_H^*F_0\cong F$, and the perfectness comparison makes $F_0$ Zariski-perfect. Apply the affine supported-extension theorem on $V$ with closed subset $T=|V|$ and open $H$. Its support hypothesis is vacuous and $V\setminus T=\varnothing$ is quasi-compact. It gives a Zariski-perfect $D_0$ on $V$ with $D_0|_H\cong F_0\oplus F_0[1]$. The perfect-quasi-coherent theorem puts $D_0$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{V,\mathrm{Zar}})$, the domain of the pullback comparison. Set $D=\epsilon_V^*D_0$, which is etale-perfect by the perfectness comparison. The equivalence's natural pullback comparison for $H\hookrightarrow V$, and its exact additive pullback, give $D|_H\cong F\oplus F[1]\cong (B\oplus B[1])|_H$.

proof.text: Invert the overlap isomorphism to obtain $c:(B\oplus B[1])|_H\xrightarrow{\sim}D|_H$. Derived gluing for the distinguished square gives $R\in D(\mathcal O_{W_2})$ and isomorphisms $e:R|_{W_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}B\oplus B[1]$ and $R|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}D$, with transition $c$. The pair $W_1\to W_2$, $V\to W_2$ is jointly surjective: the reduced closed complement $Z$ has $|Z|=|W_2|\setminus|W_1|$, the projection $V\times_{W_2}Z\to V$ identifies the points of $V\times_{W_2}Z$ with $|f|^{-1}(|Z|)$, and since $V\times_{W_2}Z\to Z$ is an isomorphism, $|f|$ maps $|f|^{-1}(|Z|)$ onto $|Z|$; so every point outside $W_1$ lifts to $V$. The object $B\oplus B[1]$ is perfect because on each common local model its terms are finite direct sums of finite-free summands, with bounded union of the shifted degree intervals. Both restrictions of $R$ therefore have the local models in the definition of perfectness, and the jointly surjective etale cover provides those models on $W_2$. Thus $R$ is perfect.

proof.text: Restrict $e$ to $U$ and put $s_2=e_U^{-1}\circ\mathrm{inl}\circ s_1$ and $r_2=r_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_1\circ e_U$. The inverse-isomorphism and biproduct identities give $r_2\circ s_2=r_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\mathrm{inl}\circ s_1=r_1\circ s_1=\mathrm{id}_A$. Hence $(R,s_2,r_2)$ witnesses $\mathcal P(W_2)$. This establishes the induction step, including compatibility of the chosen retraction with the original $A$.
